steps.notes: Spec complete (background gives mr^lh, mr^hh, (mr)^3/2 sum rule); expert impl passes all 3 tests. Note: test 2 uses x=0.6, outside the main table's stated x<0.45 validity for m_e (and the direct-gap regime), but the step prompt restates the formulas unconditionally, so not score-affecting.

Passes with SI/relative-mass interpretation, but the step is vacuously scored: all 3 targets are within np.allclose default atol=1e-8 of zero, so a constant-zero function passes officially (verified). The only operative constraint is the unstated below-gap clamp.

Passes ONLY with the reverse-engineered mixed-precision constant set e=1.6e-19, hbar=1.054571817e-34 (full CODATA), c=3e8, Eg=(1.424+1.247x) eV. True-CODATA-everything fails test 1 by 47%; natural 4-sig-fig hbar=1.0546e-34 fails at rel 4.3e-3. Test 1 sits 1-4 meV above the gap, amplifying constant rounding.

findings.evidence: h5 targets for 21.2 are {int32(0), int32(0), float64(4.359649170067458e-27)}. np.allclose default atol=1e-8 swamps the 1e-27-scale target: |0 - 4.36e-27| < 1e-8 is True, so test 2 constrains nothing. Verified with the trivial-impl probe: an alpha_eff that unconditionally returns 0 -> 'RESULT step 21.2: PASS (official joint scoring)' (review/work/21/impl_zero.py). Any unit-system choice (e.g. the natural eV-based evaluation, ~1.07e-17) also passes, as does any wrong Eg or constant set, since every plausible output magnitude is < 1e-8. The step's score carries essentially zero information about the formula alpha = C*m_r*sqrt(hbar*omega - Eg)/omega.
findings.suggested_fix: Rescale the step so the above-gap target is O(1) (e.g. define C such that the docstring's 'm^-1' claim holds, or have the test multiply by a stated constant), or add an explicit rtol-only comparison. At minimum add an above-gap test whose target magnitude exceeds atol=1e-8.

findings.evidence: Tests 0 and 1 call alpha_eff(800, 0.2, 1) and alpha_eff(980, 0, 1); both have hbar*omega < Eg (e.g. 1.553 eV < 1.673 eV for test 0), and both frozen targets are int 0. Neither the step prompt ('compute the effective absorption coefficient... alpha = C*m_r*sqrt(hbar*omega - Eg)/omega') nor the docstring says to return 0 below the bandgap. A literal implementation computes np.sqrt(negative) -> nan, and np.allclose(nan, 0) is False: verified, the no-clamp variant FAILS step 21.2 officially (isolate mode: tests 1-2 of 3 fail with AssertionError, only the above-gap test passes; review/work/21/impl_noclamp.py). The same unstated clamp is what 21.3 test 0 checks: 'assert (alpha(850, 0.2, 850, 9000) == 0) == target' with target True. Zero absorption below a direct gap is physically inferable, which keeps this at major rather than blocker, but 2 of 3 tests (and the only non-vacuous constraint of the step, see D8 finding) hinge on this unstated convention.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the 21.2 prompt/docstring: 'If hbar*omega <= Eg, the material is transparent; return 0.'

findings.evidence: Corrupted constants throughout the text a solver must use. Step 21.2 prompt: 'The electron charge is $\times 10^{-19} C$' and 'the reduced Planck constant is $\times 10^{-34} J\cdot s$' -- both mantissas stripped (only c survives: '$3\times 10^8 m/s$'). Main problem description table: 'Bandgap (eV) | + x' -- the coefficients of the canonical Casey-Panish formula Eg = 1.424 + 1.247x eV are stripped; read literally the table says Eg(0) = 0. The frozen targets (verified by constant-scan, review/work/21/scan_constants.py) require Eg = 1.424 + 1.247x, e = 1.6e-19, hbar = 1.054571817e-34. For 21.2 itself the scoring impact is masked by the atol blind spot (D8 finding: any constants pass), but the spec as written is unrecoverable without outside literature knowledge; the scoring damage lands on 21.3 (see blocker there).
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the stripped numbers: bandgap row '1.424 + 1.247x (x < 0.45)'; '1.6e-19 C'; and state hbar to the precision the target actually uses (1.054571817e-34 J s).

findings.evidence: The 21.3 targets are reproducible ONLY with the mixed-precision constant set e=1.6e-19 (2 s.f.), hbar=1.054571817e-34 (10-digit CODATA, i.e. scipy.constants.hbar), c=3e8 (1 s.f.), Eg=(1.424+1.247x) eV -- rel errors 2.6e-6/1.7e-7/2.5e-7 -> PASS (review/work/21/impl_winning.py). Competent alternatives fail officially (verified): (a) true CODATA everything (e=1.602176634e-19, c=299792458): values [1499.06, 15330.5, 20963.36] vs targets [2835.34, 14978.72, 20275.48], rel errors 4.7e-1/2.3e-2/3.4e-2 -> FAIL; (b) the natural 4-sig-fig hbar=1.0546e-34 with e=1.6e-19, c=3e8: rel errors 4.3e-3/2.9e-4/4.1e-4 -> FAIL at rtol 1e-5. Root causes compound: the prompt's constant mantissas are stripped (see 21.2 D2 finding), the required precision mix is internally inconsistent (full-precision hbar next to 1-2 s.f. e and c), and test 1 (lambda=800, x=0.1) sits only hbar*omega-Eg = 4.28 meV (author constants) vs 1.10 meV (true constants) above the gap, so sqrt of that sliver amplifies constant rounding into a 47% miss. A solver passes only by the specific lucky guess 'exact scipy hbar + rounded e=1.6e-19 + c=3e8'; both self-consistent choices (all-rounded or all-exact) fail.
findings.suggested_fix: State all three constants in the prompt exactly as used to generate the target (e=1.6e-19, hbar=1.054571817e-34, c=3e8) AND restore the Eg formula; ideally also move test 1 away from the band edge (e.g. lambda=750) or loosen tolerance, since meV-level proximity to the gap makes the test ill-conditioned in the constants.

findings.evidence: Header 'def alpha_eff(lambda_i, x, C):' has no default for C, but the docstring says 'C (float): Optional scaling factor... Default is 1.' and the 21.3 prompt refers to 'the previous function alpha_eff(lambda, x, C=1)'. Tests always pass C explicitly, and step 3 is written by the same solver, so this cannot flip a score by itself.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the header to def alpha_eff(lambda_i, x, C=1).

overall_assessment: Not fair to score as-is. Step 21.1 is clean, but 21.2 and 21.3 are broken in opposite directions: 21.2's targets (0, 0, 4.36e-27) all fall under np.allclose's default atol, so a constant-zero implementation passes officially while a literal implementation of the given formula (no below-gap clamp) fails with nan; 21.3's targets encode an internally inconsistent mixed-precision constant set (rounded e and c, 10-digit CODATA hbar) whose mantissas are stripped from the prompt, with a near-band-edge test point that turns constant rounding into a 47% miss for true CODATA values. A competent solver would most likely score 1/3 on this problem despite fully understanding the physics.
